title: Browse Chronic Special Needs plans
summary: Explains UnitedHealthcare Chronic Special Needs plans (C-SNPs) for people with diabetes, chronic heart failure or cardiovascular disorders, including benefits, eligibility and enrollment periods.

atoms.title: What a Chronic Special Needs plan is
atoms.question: What is a Chronic Special Needs plan?
atoms.text: A UnitedHealthcare Chronic Special Needs plan (C-SNP) is a Medicare Advantage plan designed for people living with qualifying chronic conditions: diabetes, chronic heart failure and cardiovascular disorders.

atoms.title: Benefits of UnitedHealthcare C-SNPs
atoms.question: What benefits can a UnitedHealthcare C-SNP include?
atoms.text: A UnitedHealthcare C-SNP offers coverage and guidance, and benefits may include $0 annual physical exams, $0 lab tests and $0 preventive care; a large network of Medicare Advantage providers; $0 copay on dental, vision and hearing exams; a UCard with a monthly credit to help pay for OTC products and healthy food; $0 diabetic supplies plus foot care and diabetic shoes; and a 1-month supply of covered insulin for $25 or less. Plan availability and coverage may vary by service area.

atoms.title: Who a C-SNP is and isn't right for
atoms.question: Is a C-SNP right for me?
atoms.text: A C-SNP might be right if you have diabetes, chronic heart failure and/or cardiovascular disorders, would benefit from extra care management programs to support your health, and would like added benefits and features at no extra cost. It might not be right if you are eligible for a Dual Special Needs plan (D-SNP) in your area, you do not have a qualifying chronic condition, or you live outside an eligible plan coverage area.

atoms.title: What a C-SNP covers
atoms.question: What does a Chronic Special Needs plan cover?
atoms.text: A UnitedHealthcare C-SNP provides all the coverage of Original Medicare (Part A and Part B), prescription drug coverage, condition care management and low specialist copays. A C-SNP typically offers many extras like dental, hearing and vision benefits. All SNPs include prescription drug coverage, and plan availability depends on where you live.

atoms.title: C-SNP versus D-SNP
atoms.question: What is the difference between a C-SNP and a D-SNP?
atoms.text: Both plan types provide all the benefits of Original Medicare, plus prescription drug coverage. A C-SNP includes care management for chronic conditions, while a D-SNP offers coordination between Medicare and Medicaid, intended to deliver benefits at lower cost to the member.

atoms.title: Who is eligible for a C-SNP
atoms.question: Who is eligible for a Chronic Special Needs plan?
atoms.text: To enroll in a C-SNP, you must be eligible for Medicare Part A and Part B and have a qualifying health condition. You will need to complete a chronic condition verification form with help from your doctor within 60 days of the plan's start date. UnitedHealthcare C-SNPs are designed for people with diabetes, chronic heart failure or cardiovascular disorders.

atoms.title: I-SNPs, IE-SNPs and D-SNPs as other SNP types
atoms.question: What other Special Needs plans are available besides C-SNPs?
atoms.text: Dual Special Needs plans (D-SNPs) are for people who have both Medicare and Medicaid coverage and help coordinate benefits with Medicaid. Institutional Special Needs plans (I-SNPs) are for people who live in a long term care setting, such as a skilled nursing facility. Institutional Equivalent Special Needs plans (IE-SNPs) are for people who receive skilled nursing care at home or in assisted living. All SNPs include prescription drug coverage.

atoms.title: When there is no C-SNP in your area
atoms.question: What if there are no C-SNPs where I live?
atoms.text: If a Chronic Special Needs plan is not available in your area, another Medicare Advantage plan may be a good fit.

atoms.title: When you can enroll in a C-SNP
atoms.question: When can I enroll in a C-SNP plan?
atoms.text: You can enroll during: 1) your Initial Enrollment Period, the 7-month period starting three months before the month of your 65th birthday and ending three months after; 2) the Annual Enrollment Period, October 15 to December 7; 3) the General Enrollment Period, January 1 to March 31, for signing up for Original Medicare, followed by Medicare Advantage enrollment April through June; 4) the Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period, January 1 to March 31; or 5) the Chronic Condition Special Enrollment Period.

atoms.title: Chronic Condition Special Enrollment Period
atoms.question: What is the Chronic Condition Special Enrollment Period?
atoms.text: The Chronic Condition Special Enrollment Period is open any time for people with severe or disabling chronic conditions covered by an available Special Needs plan. It is only allowed for enrolling in a C-SNP, and only if you do not already have a C-SNP serving the same condition. All Special Needs plans are Medicare Advantage plans.
